title: Place kernels on a roofline
goal:
Use the roofline to place kernels on a machine. Each kernel is a `(name, flops, bytes)` tuple. `peak` is in FLOP/s and `bw` is in bytes/s (use base units here, not GFLOP/s).

- `place(kernels, peak, bw)` returns a list of dicts, one per kernel and in the same order. Each dict has `name`, `intensity` (FLOPs per byte), `regime` (`"memory"` or `"compute"`), `attainable` (FLOP/s from the roofline), and `time` (seconds).
- `time` is the lower bound `max(flops / peak, bytes / bw)`. It must agree with `flops / attainable`. The two views of the roofline are the same model.
- A kernel at exactly the ridge point counts as `"compute"`.
hints: A kernel needs at least `flops / peak` seconds to compute and `bytes / bw` seconds to move its data. Whichever is longer is the bound, and it names the regime.
`attainable = min(peak, bw * intensity)`. Check that `flops / attainable` equals your `time`.
Keep the input order. Don't sort the kernels.
